cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Frontal bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with parietal, sphenoid, ethmoid, nasal, maxillary, lacrimal and zygomatic bones.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Frontal squama, orbital plates, supraorbital margins/notches and frontal sinus region.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the forehead, orbital roofs and part of the anterior cranial fossa.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Nasal bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with frontal bone, maxilla and the opposite nasal bone.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the superior bony bridge of the external nose.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Small paired rectangular bones forming the nasal bridge.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ethmoid bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with frontal, sphenoid, vomer, nasal, maxillary, lacrimal, palatine bones and inferior nasal conchae.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Cribriform plate, crista galli, perpendicular plate, superior and middle nasal conchae and ethmoidal labyrinths.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Contributes to the anterior cranial floor, nasal septum and medial orbital wall.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sphenoid bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital, ethmoid, zygomatic, vomer and palatine bones.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Body, greater and lesser wings, pterygoid processes, sella turcica, foramina rotundum and ovale.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Central bone of skull base; contributes to orbit, cranial fossae and pterygopalatine/infratemporal regions.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Maxilla

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with multiple facial bones and contributes to the hard palate, nasal cavity and orbit.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Alveolar process, palatine process, infraorbital foramen and maxillary sinus.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Houses the upper teeth and forms much of the midface.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Palatine bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with maxilla, sphenoid, ethmoid, vomer, inferior nasal concha and opposite palatine bone.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Horizontal plate forms posterior hard palate; perpendicular plate contributes to lateral nasal wall.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Horizontal plate, perpendicular plate, pyramidal process and greater/lesser palatine foramina.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Mandible

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with the temporal bones at the temporomandibular joints.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Body, ramus, angle, coronoid process, condylar process, mental foramen and mandibular foramen.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Supports lower teeth and provides major attachments for muscles of mastication and floor of mouth.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Hyoid

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Does not articulate directly with other bones; suspended by muscles and ligaments.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Body, greater horns and lesser horns.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Located in the anterior neck between the mandible and thyroid cartilage.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral nasal cartilage

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Paired hyaline cartilage forming part of the upper lateral wall of the external nose.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies inferior to nasal bone and superior to the major alar cartilage.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Supports the lateral nasal wall and helps maintain patency of the nasal airway.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Thyroid cartilage

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Largest laryngeal cartilage, formed by two laminae meeting anteriorly.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Laryngeal prominence, superior/inferior horns and oblique line.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Protects the vocal apparatus and provides attachment for laryngeal muscles and ligaments.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior nasal concha

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Curved bony projection from the ethmoid bone on the superior lateral nasal wall.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Increases mucosal surface area and promotes warming, humidification and turbulence of inspired air.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Overlies the superior meatus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Middle nasal concha

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Curved bony projection from the ethmoid bone on the lateral nasal wall.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Increases mucosal surface area and influences airflow around paranasal sinus drainage pathways.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Overlies the middle meatus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior nasal concha

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Separate paired bone projecting from the inferior lateral nasal wall.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Increases mucosal surface area and promotes warming and humidification of inspired air.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Overlies the inferior meatus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Palatine tonsil

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Lies in the tonsillar fossa between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Part of Waldeyer's ring and contributes to mucosal immune surveillance.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Glossopharyngeal nerve and tonsillar vessels lie close to the tonsillar bed.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Mylohyoid muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Elevates the floor of mouth and hyoid during swallowing; assists depression of the mandible when the hyoid is fixed.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to mylohyoid from the inferior alveolar nerve (V3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Mylohyoid line of mandible.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Median mylohyoid raphe and body of hyoid.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Geniohyoid muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Pulls the hyoid anterosuperiorly and shortens the floor of mouth; can assist mandibular depression.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: C1 fibres travelling with the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Inferior mental spine of mandible.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Body of hyoid.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sublingual gland

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Produces predominantly mucous saliva.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Floor of mouth beneath the mucosa, superior to mylohyoid and lateral to genioglossus.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Multiple small ducts open along the sublingual fold; a larger duct may join the submandibular duct.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Parasympathetic secretomotor fibres from facial nerve via chorda tympani, lingual nerve and submandibular ganglion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Submandibular gland

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Produces mixed serous and mucous saliva, predominantly serous.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Wraps around the posterior border of mylohyoid with superficial and deep parts.

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Submandibular duct opens at the sublingual papilla beside the lingual frenulum.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Parasympathetic secretomotor fibres from facial nerve via chorda tympani, lingual nerve and submandibular ganglion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common carotid artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Right arises from brachiocephalic trunk; left arises directly from aortic arch.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends in the carotid sheath and usually bifurcates around the upper border of thyroid cartilage into internal and external carotid arteries.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: No major branches in the neck before its terminal bifurcation.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Supplies head and neck through the external and internal carotid systems.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External carotid artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of common carotid artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends through the carotid triangle, passes deep to posterior belly of digastric and enters parotid gland.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Superior thyroid, ascending pharyngeal, lingual, facial, occipital, posterior auricular, maxillary and superficial temporal arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Most extracranial structures of head and neck.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Internal carotid artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of common carotid artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends in carotid sheath without branching in the neck, enters carotid canal and continues intracranially.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Major arterial supply to the brain and orbit.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies posterolateral to the external carotid near the bifurcation before ascending deep in the neck.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Greater palatine artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of the descending palatine artery from the maxillary artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends through the greater palatine canal, emerges at the greater palatine foramen and runs anteriorly on the hard palate.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Hard palate, palatal gingiva and adjacent structures.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Anastomoses anteriorly with the septal branch of the sphenopalatine artery via incisive canal region.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Optic nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Special sensory fibres from retinal ganglion cells; functionally part of the CNS.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Leaves the orbit through the optic canal and reaches the optic chiasm.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Vision.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Lesion causes ipsilateral monocular visual loss and an afferent pupillary defect.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Trigeminal nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Large sensory root and smaller motor root emerging from the lateral pons.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Sensory root expands into the trigeminal ganglion; V1, V2 and V3 then leave the cranial cavity by different foramina.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Motor fibres travel with V3 to muscles of mastication and selected first-pharyngeal-arch muscles.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Major somatic sensory nerve of face, oral/nasal cavities, teeth, cornea and much of cranial dura.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: May cause ipsilateral facial sensory loss; motor root involvement causes weakness of mastication with the jaw deviating toward the side of the lesion on opening; the corneal reflex afferent limb may be impaired if V1 is involved.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Trigeminal ganglion

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Lies in Meckel's cave near the apex of the petrous temporal bone.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Contains sensory neuron cell bodies of the trigeminal nerve.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Gives rise to ophthalmic (V1), maxillary (V2) and mandibular (V3) divisions.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ophthalmic nerve

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and exits through the superior orbital fissure.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies cornea, upper eyelid, forehead, scalp, dorsum of nose and parts of nasal cavity and cranial dura.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: None; purely sensory.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes sensory loss over the forehead, cornea and dorsum of the nose, with loss or reduction of the afferent limb of the corneal reflex.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Maxillary nerve

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus, exits via foramen rotundum and enters the pterygopalatine fossa.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies midface, upper lip, maxillary teeth, palate and parts of nasal cavity.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: None; purely sensory.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes sensory loss or paraesthesia over the midface, upper lip, maxillary teeth and palate; there is no motor deficit because V2 is purely sensory.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Mandibular nerve

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Exits cranial cavity through foramen ovale and enters the infratemporal fossa.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies muscles of mastication, mylohyoid, anterior belly of digastric, tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies lower face, mandibular teeth, anterior two-thirds of tongue for general sensation and parts of external ear and dura.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes sensory loss over the lower face, mandibular teeth and general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue; motor involvement weakens mastication and the jaw deviates toward the affected side on opening.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Olfactory nerves

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Special sensory fibres from olfactory receptor neurons in the olfactory epithelium.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Small fascicles pass through foramina in the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Smell.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Injury may cause anosmia and can occur with cribriform plate fractures.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Palatine nerves

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Branches associated with the maxillary nerve via the pterygopalatine ganglion.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descend through the palatine canals to the palate as greater and lesser palatine nerves.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: General sensation from much of the hard and soft palate.

cards.question: Parasympathetic functions
cards.answer: Carry postganglionic parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to palatal glands.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Anterior ethmoidal nerve (branch of the ophthalmic nerve)

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Branch of the nasociliary nerve from ophthalmic division of trigeminal nerve (V1).

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through anterior ethmoidal foramen into anterior cranial fossa, then through cribriform region into nasal cavity.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies anterosuperior nasal cavity and skin of lower dorsum/tip of nose via external nasal branch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Greater palatine nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Branch of maxillary nerve distribution via the pterygopalatine ganglion.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends through greater palatine canal and emerges through greater palatine foramen to run anteriorly on hard palate.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies most of the hard palate and palatal gingiva.

cards.question: Parasympathetic functions
cards.answer: Carries postganglionic secretomotor fibres to palatal glands.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Nasopalatine nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Branch of maxillary nerve distribution via the pterygopalatine ganglion.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Enters nasal cavity through sphenopalatine foramen, crosses nasal septum and passes through incisive canal.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies posterior/inferior nasal septum and anterior hard palate behind the incisors.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lingual nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Branch of posterior division of mandibular nerve (V3).

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends in infratemporal fossa, passes close to mandibular third molar, then runs in floor of mouth around the submandibular duct.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: General sensation from anterior two-thirds of tongue, floor of mouth and lingual gingiva.

cards.question: Parasympathetic functions
cards.answer: Carries chorda tympani taste fibres and preganglionic parasympathetic fibres to the submandibular ganglion.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Can cause loss of general sensation and taste from anterior tongue and reduced salivary secretion depending on lesion site.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pterygopalatine ganglion

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Lies in the pterygopalatine fossa, suspended from the maxillary nerve.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Parasympathetic ganglion for lacrimal, nasal and palatal gland secretomotor pathways.

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibres arrive via greater petrosal nerve and nerve of pterygoid canal; sympathetic and sensory fibres pass through without synapsing.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Distributes fibres through branches of V2, including palatine and nasal branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vagus nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Medullary nuclei including nucleus ambiguus, dorsal motor nucleus of vagus and nucleus solitarius pathways.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Emerges from postolivary sulcus, exits through jugular foramen and descends in the carotid sheath.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies most muscles of the palate, pharynx and larynx.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Visceral sensation from thoracoabdominal organs and sensation from larynx/pharynx; taste from epiglottic region.

cards.question: Parasympathetic functions
cards.answer: Provides parasympathetic supply to thoracic and much of abdominal viscera.

cards.question: Note
cards.answer: May have fallen off the physical model.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: May cause dysphagia and hoarseness, ipsilateral palatal weakness with the uvula deviating away from the lesion, and loss of the efferent limb of the gag reflex.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Hypoglossal nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Hypoglossal nucleus in the medulla.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Emerges between pyramid and olive, exits via hypoglossal canal and passes toward the tongue.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies intrinsic and extrinsic tongue muscles except palatoglossus.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Lower motor neuron lesion causes ipsilateral tongue weakness, atrophy and deviation toward the lesion on protrusion.
